headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading error: browser/MCP document agent can exfiltrate or act on Authelia-authenticated content without strong provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can front authentication flows via OIDC/OAuth2 and ForwardAuth, while next-ai-draw-io ingests natural-language commands and uses MCP/browser-based workflows. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one side can be treated as instructions by the other, especially if shared files or pasted outputs are involved. No direct shared channel is documented, so I do not escalate further.
conditions: IF outputs from Authelia-protected pages are copied into next-ai-draw-io prompts
IF next-ai-draw-io reads files or pasted text from a shared workspace as instructions
mitigations: Separate prompt inputs from copied web content
Disable automatic ingestion of pasted HTML/text
Use a provenance tag for all imported snippets
Review any MCP tool calls before execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia handles authentication traffic and broad network egress, while next-ai-draw-io touches PDFs, text, images, and diagram files and can send context to multiple third-party model APIs. If sensitive documents or auth-related artifacts enter the document agent, its default API-backed processing can leak them outside the local boundary. The pairwise risk is driven by next-ai-draw-io; Authelia adds the sensitive access path.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are opened in next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to use a remote model provider
mitigations: Use a local-only model backend
Restrict the document set to non-sensitive files
Turn off cloud API keys for the session
Store auth artifacts outside the shared workspace
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/OIDC-facing behavior, while next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances and uses MCP plus external model APIs. Their write surfaces are not explicitly shared, so a direct filesystem conflict is not proven; however, overlapping mutable external resources and concurrent instances make coordination failures plausible. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same OAuth-backed resource
IF both agents modify the same external document or diagram store without locking
mitigations: Assign separate credentials per agent
Avoid shared mutable workspaces
Serialize edits to the same resource
Check for duplicate instance launches
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io explicitly uses natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization, so it may treat upstream content as authoritative. Authelia can supply identity or access-related outputs that the document agent could render or act on without verification. That creates a default-path cascade from authentication context into generated diagrams or actions, with potentially incorrect downstream decisions.
conditions: IF Authelia-derived text is fed into next-ai-draw-io as source material
IF next-ai-draw-io generates diagrams or actions without a verification step
mitigations: Require human review before export
Mark upstream text as untrusted by default
Compare generated output against source documents
Limit automation to read-only drafts
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication layer and next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, images, and diagrams while handling API keys and environment variables. Even without a documented residency mismatch, the pair can place regulated or sensitive identity-linked content into a third-party model workflow, creating retention and subject-rights ambiguity. I cite both because the compliance risk arises from their combined handling path.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through next-ai-draw-io
IF identity-linked content from Authelia is included in those documents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the document agent
Use a local retention policy for exports
Rotate API keys after sensitive sessions
Document which data classes may be processed
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls per provider
